NCT05918211.what_is_this_study_about: FUEL-2 is studying whether udenafil, a medicine taken by mouth, can safely improve exercise capacity in teens with single ventricle heart disease who have had the Fontan procedure. Participants are assigned by chance to udenafil or a placebo (a look-alike tablet with no active medicine), with an equal chance of either. Participants, families, and study clinicians do not know which treatment a participant receives. Researchers compare exercise testing at the beginning and after 26 weeks to measure changes in how much oxygen the body uses during maximum effort.
NCT05918211.who_might_this_be_for: Teens ages 12 through 18 with Fontan circulation may qualify. Participants must be at least 132 cm tall (about 4 feet 4 inches), weigh at least 40 kg (about 88 pounds), and already take an antiplatelet or anticoagulant medicine to help prevent blood clots. They must be able to complete exercise testing and meet specific exercise-capacity requirements. Some health conditions and medicines may rule out participation, including recent hospitalization for worsening heart failure, transplant evaluation or listing, and recent ongoing use of a PDE5 inhibitor. These are selected criteria; the study team reviews the full requirements and determines eligibility.
NCT05918211.why_might_this_matter: Exercise can be challenging for some people with Fontan circulation. This study asks whether udenafil could help teens exercise more effectively while evaluating its safety. Researchers also measure exercise performance below maximum effort and blood markers related to liver scarring. Benefit is not established by this study description, and participation may not improve a teen's symptoms or exercise ability.
NCT05918211.what_should_families_know: Participation includes about six months of treatment and exercise testing at the start and end. According to fuel2study.com, participants take udenafil or placebo twice daily, travel-related expenses are covered, and additional compensation may be available. Families should confirm visit schedules, travel arrangements, compensation, and possible side effects with the study team. Consent is required, including parent or guardian permission and the teen's assent when applicable. The study website offers an interest form to connect families with a recruitment coordinator. This summary draws on the supplied ClinicalTrials.gov record for NCT05918211 and fuel2study.com; the full eligibility criteria and study-team discussion remain essential.
